questions.problem:
The time that a particular laptop battery lasts is normally distributed with a mean of $32$ hours and a standard deviation of $4$ hours. What is the probability that a full charge lasts for $36$ hours or more? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8159\,$ | $\,0.8186\,$ | $\,0.8212\,$ |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8413\,$ | $\,0.8438\,$ | $\,0.8461\,$ |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8643\,$ | $\,0.8665\,$ | $\,0.8686\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the time the full charge lasts. Then we have $X∼N(32,{4}^{2}).$

We want to find $P(X\ge 36).$ Thus, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 36) & =P(Z\ge \frac{36-32}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge 1) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1) \\  & =1-Φ(1)\end{aligned}
$$

From the $z$-table, we see that

$$
1-Φ(1)=1-0.8413≈0.1587.
$$

Therefore, the probability that a full charge lasts $36$ hours or more is approximately $0.16.$

questions.problem:
A group of students took a test and got an average score of $79.$ Also, $15%$ of the students scored lower than $66.$ Assuming that the scores of the students are normally distributed, find the standard deviation of their scores, rounded to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the grade obtained by a student. Then we have $X∼N(79,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X\le 66)=0.15.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 66) & =0.15 \\ P(Z\le \frac{66-79}{\sigma }) & =0.15 \\ Φ(-\frac{13}{\sigma }) & =0.15 \\ -\frac{13}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.15).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.85)=1.0364,
$$

and therefore by symmetry, we have

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(1-0.85)={Φ}^{-1}(0.15)=-1.0364.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{13}{\sigma } & =-1.0364 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{-13}{-1.0364} \\  & ≈12.54.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A truck travels an average distance of $21\,\text{mi}$ with a gallon of gas. However, $15%$ of the time, a truck travels more than $26\,\text{mi}$ on a gallon of gas. Assuming that the distance the truck can travel with a gallon of gas is normally distributed, find, as a percent, the proportion of journeys that the truck travels less than $15\,\text{mi}$ on a gallon of gas. Round your answer to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.3\,$ | $\,0.0918\,$ | $\,0.0901\,$ | $\,0.0885\,$ |
| $\,-1.2\,$ | $\,0.1093\,$ | $\,0.1075\,$ | $\,0.1056\,$ |
| $\,-1.1\,$ | $\,0.1292\,$ | $\,0.1271\,$ | $\,0.1251\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the distance traveled by the truck with a gallon of gas. Then we have $X∼N(21,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X\le 15).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X>26)=0.15.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 26) & =1-P(X>26) \\  & =1-0.15 \\  & =0.85\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 26) & =0.85 \\ P(Z\le \frac{26-21}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ Φ(\frac{5}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ \frac{5}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.85)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.85)≈1.0364.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{\sigma } & =1.0364 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & =0.2073 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1}{0.2073} \\  & ≈4.8239.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X\le 15)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 15) & =P(Z\le \frac{15-21}{4.8239}) \\  & ≈P(Z\le -1.24) \\  & =Φ(-1.24) \\  & =0.1075 \\  & ≈10.8%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $10.8%$ of the time, a gallon of gas travels only $15\,\text{mi}$ or less.

questions.problem:
The average height of a player in a particular professional basketball league is $78$ inches. Additionally, $15%$ of players are over $82$ inches tall. Assuming that a player's height is normally distributed, find the percentage of players over $75$ inches tall, rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.75\,$ | $\,0.80\,$ | $\,0.85\,$ | $\,0.90\,$ | $\,0.95\,$ | $\,0.97\,$ | $\,0.99\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.8808\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1660\,$ | $\,0.1635\,$ | $\,0.1611\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.1922\,$ | $\,0.1894\,$ | $\,0.1867\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2206\,$ | $\,0.2177\,$ | $\,0.2148\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the height of a randomly selected player. Then we have $X∼N(78,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X>75).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X>82)=0.15.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 82) & =1-P(X>82) \\  & =1-0.15 \\  & =0.85\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 82) & =0.85 \\ P(Z\le \frac{82-78}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ Φ(\frac{4}{\sigma }) & =0.85 \\ \frac{4}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.85)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.85)≈1.0364.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{\sigma } & =1.0364 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & =0.2591 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1}{0.2591} \\  & ≈3.85951.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X>75)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>75) & =1-P(X\le 75) \\  & =1-P(Z\le \frac{75-78}{3.85951}) \\  & ≈1-P(Z\le -0.78) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.78) \\  & =1-0.2177 \\  & =0.7823 \\  & ≈78.2%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $78.2%$ of players are over $75$ inch tall.

questions.problem:
The lifespan of LED light bulbs is normally distributed with a mean of $40,000$ hours and an unknown standard deviation $\sigma .$ Tests show that $10%$ of bulbs fail before $36,000$ hours. Assuming a normal model, find the standard deviation, **rounded to the nearest integer.**

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $\,z\,$ | $0.75$ | $0.8$ | $0.85$ | $0.9$ | $0.95$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ |

$\sigma ≈$
{{field-1}}
$h$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the lifespan of an LED bulb. Then we have $X∼N(40,000,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X<36,000)=0.10.$ Converting $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<36,000) & =0.10 \\ P(Z\le \frac{36,000-40,000}{\sigma }) & =0.10 \\ Φ(-\frac{4,000}{\sigma }) & =0.10 \\ -\frac{4,000}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.10).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.9)=1.2816,
$$

and therefore, by symmetry, we have

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.10)=-1.2816.
$$

Finally then, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{4,000}{\sigma } & =-1.2816 \\ \frac{4,000}{\sigma } & =1.2816 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{4,000}{1.2816} \\ \sigma  & ≈3,121\,\text{h.}\end{aligned}
$$
